body_es: `git cherry-pick` toma el cambio introducido por un commit específico de una rama y lo aplica como un nuevo commit sobre otra rama, sin traer el resto del historial de la rama de origen. Es distinto de un merge, que integra todos los commits de una rama; cherry-pick es quirúrgico y solo mueve uno (o unos pocos, indicados uno a uno). El caso típico es un fix crítico que se hizo en `develop` y que necesita llegar a `master` de inmediato, sin arrastrar features a medio terminar que también viven en `develop`. Internamente, Git calcula el diff que introdujo ese commit y lo reaplica sobre el estado actual de la rama destino, generando un commit nuevo con un hash distinto pero el mismo contenido de cambio. Si el cherry-pick genera conflictos, Git los presenta como en un merge normal, y se resuelven con `git cherry-pick --continue` tras arreglarlos, o se cancela todo con `--abort`. Un error común es hacer cherry-pick del mismo commit dos veces hacia la misma rama por distintos caminos, lo que puede duplicar el cambio o complicar un merge posterior si Git no reconoce que ya se aplicó.
body_en: `git cherry-pick` takes the change introduced by a specific commit on one branch and applies it as a new commit on another branch, without bringing along the rest of the source branch's history. It differs from a merge, which integrates every commit from a branch; cherry-pick is surgical and moves only one commit (or a few, specified one by one). The typical case is a critical fix made on `develop` that needs to reach `master` immediately, without dragging along half-finished features that also live on `develop`. Internally, Git computes the diff introduced by that commit and reapplies it on top of the target branch's current state, producing a new commit with a different hash but the same change content. If the cherry-pick causes conflicts, Git presents them just as in a normal merge, and you resolve them with `git cherry-pick --continue` after fixing them, or cancel everything with `--abort`. A common mistake is cherry-picking the same commit twice onto the same branch through different paths, which can duplicate the change or complicate a later merge if Git does not recognize it was already applied.
example_code:
class Commit:
    def __init__(self, sha, message, change):
        self.sha = sha
        self.message = message
        self.change = change


def cherry_pick(commit, target_branch, next_sha):
    new_commit = Commit(next_sha, commit.message, commit.change)
    target_branch.append(new_commit)
    return new_commit


develop = [
    Commit("3z4y5x6", "Update dependencies", "package.json"),
    Commit("4a5b6c7", "Add logging", "logger.py"),
    Commit("5x6y7z8", "Fix critical bug in auth", "auth.py"),
]
master = [Commit("1a2b3c4", "Initial release", "README.md")]

fix = next(c for c in develop if "Fix critical" in c.message)
picked = cherry_pick(fix, master, "9k0l1m2")

for c in master:
    print(f"{c.sha} {c.message} ({c.change})")
print("mismo cambio, distinto hash:", fix.sha != picked.sha, picked.change == fix.change)

9k0l1m2 Fix critical bug in auth (auth.py)
mismo cambio, distinto hash: True True
